title: First-run setup for a company database, with the company settings, module set and environment stored in the database for every user
status: delivered beyond the 130-feature plan - the plan count is unchanged and this capability is recorded in addition to it
scope: the first-run wizard mirrors the ERP's six steps and hosts the shared connection catalogue, connection editor and the two downloaders
two deployments: a local database file on this workstation, or a company database on a server
a company database keeps its settings in the database (BEEPSETTINGS), prepared by the system administrator, read by every user at start
settings are one JSON row per document: the company record, the PPDM module set, and the Oil & Gas environment
only the SystemAdmin prepares and changes them; every other user reads them
the SECURITY module now runs in the desktop setup, so the company database gets the USER/ROLE/PERMISSION tables and its default roles

implementation.passwordPolicy: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Core/OgPasswordPolicy.cs (one rule for the workstation store and a company account)

table.name: BEEPSETTINGS
table.columns: SETTINGS_ID (PK), SETTINGS_JSON (1 MB), REVISION, PREVIOUS_REVISION, INTENT_ID, UPDATED_BY, UPDATED_UTC + the ModelEntityBase audit columns
table.created_by: the first administrator's setup run, through the engine's schema provider from the entity class (no statement text in the desktop)

tests.name: SharedSetupIntegrationTests.The_company_record_is_created_by_the_first_run_and_a_stale_write_is_refused
tests.proves: a database with no settings table says so and reading does not create it; the first save creates BEEPSETTINGS and records the company; a second workstation writing with the revision it did not see is refused (settings-record-changed); the administrator who did read it can change it

tests.name: SharedSetupIntegrationTests.The_module_set_and_the_environment_document_round_trip
tests.proves: the module set and the shared environment document survive a real database round trip

tests.name: SharedSetupIntegrationTests.An_installation_document_that_cannot_be_read_is_refused_rather_than_half_applied
tests.proves: an unreadable or blank company document is 'not recorded', is recorded as a degraded failure, and is never adopted as a company with empty values

tests.name: SharedSetupIntegrationTests.The_module_document_survives_a_document_a_later_build_may_write
tests.proves: an unknown module document reads as an empty set instead of throwing

tests.name: SourceGuardTests.Company_settings_are_one_database_table_and_only_the_system_administrator_prepares_them
tests.proves: the table is BEEPSETTINGS, the settings page gate is Permissions.IsSystemAdmin, and the setup composition discovers SECURITY and registers its seed service

tests.name: DatabaseIdentityTests.An_administrator_is_created_in_the_database_and_can_sign_in_with_the_roles_it_grants
tests.proves: the wizard creates the account in the company database; the stored password is a pbkdf2-sha256 envelope and never the password; signing in returns the Administrator role read from USER_ROLE

tests.name: DatabaseIdentityTests.A_wrong_password_and_an_unknown_user_get_the_same_sentence_and_no_session
tests.proves: the sign-in screen cannot enumerate accounts

tests.name: DatabaseIdentityTests.A_seeded_principal_is_not_a_login_account
tests.proves: the security module's seeded principals ('seeded-no-login') never authenticate

tests.name: DatabaseIdentityTests.Creating_a_second_account_with_the_same_name_is_refused
tests.proves: a workstation joining an existing company does not recreate the administrator

tests.name: DatabaseIdentityTests.The_password_policy_is_one_rule_for_every_account_store
tests.proves: the workstation and the company database hold an account to the same rule

limits: there is no enterprise server in this environment, so a server connection (EnsureRemoteAsync) is compiled and reviewed but not exercised against SQL Server, PostgreSQL or Oracle

the company account is created with the security module's own business associate (BEEP_USER_SYSTEM), because that is the principal the seeded roles belong to; per-company business associates and a user-management screen are not built yet

the environment document stored in TOOLS_ENVIRONMENT names the country preset and unit system rather than a resolved copy: the presets ship with the application, so the document records the choice and the engine supplies the values (a resolved copy measured 1.2 MB and would drift from the shipped presets)
the wizard's own text is English, like the window it replaces; the settings it writes are culture-aware and the interface language is applied from the record
orderOfEvents: the workstation holds only machine facts: which deployment and which connection (setup.json + the encrypted connection definition)
before anybody signs in, no company setting is read
sign-in for a company deployment is against the company database USER table (PBKDF2-SHA256 verifier) and the roles come from USER_ROLE/ROLE
only after a successful sign-in are the company settings (BEEPSETTINGS) and the shared environment read, and the role set applied to the session
the shell opens with that company and that user's rights
